1:# Clever Cloud Logs Drains
3:You can use Clever Tools to control logs drains, through following commands. Each can target a specific application, adding `--app APP_ID_OR_NAME` or a local alias (`--alias`, `-a`):
6:clever drain
7:clever drain -F json
8:clever drain create <DRAIN-TYPE> <DRAIN-URL>
9:clever drain get <DRAIN-ID>
10:clever drain get <DRAIN-ID> --format json
11:clever drain remove <DRAIN-ID>
12:clever drain enable <DRAIN-ID>
13:clever drain disable <DRAIN-ID>
16:Where `DRAIN-TYPE` is one of:
26:Drain creation supports the following options:
33:[--sd-params, -s] SD_PARAMS           RFC5424 structured data parameters (for ovh-tcp), e.g.: `X-OVH-TOKEN=\"REDACTED\"`
36:## ElasticSearch logs drains
38:ElasticSearch drains use the Elastic bulk API. To match this endpoint, specify `/_bulk` at the end of your ElasticSearch endpoint.
40:## Datadog logs drains
44:To create a [Datadog](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/?lang=python#send-logs-over-http) drain, you just need to use one of the following command depending on your zone:
48:clever drain create DatadogHTTP "https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.eu/v1/input/<API_KEY>?ddsource=clevercloud&service=<SERVICE>&host=<HOST>"
50:clever drain create DatadogHTTP "https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input/<API_KEY>?ddsource=clevercloud&service=<SERVICE>&host=<HOST>"
55:## NewRelic logs drains
59:To create a [NewRelic](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/logs/log-api/introduction-log-api/) drain, you just need to use:
62:clever drain create NewRelicHTTP "https://log-api.eu.newrelic.com/log/v1" --api-key <API_KEY>

I haven't made any changes yet. One thing blocks me: I can't confirm what the Clever Cloud drains API expects for a Splunk drain.

**What I found**
- Every drain type is declared in `DRAIN_TYPES` (`src/models/drain.js:18`). Each has an `apiCode`, which is sent as `recipient.type` to `POST /v4/drains/...`. The type-specific fields are set in `src/commands/drain/drain.create.command.js`, for example `apiKey` for New Relic and `sourceToken` for Better Stack.
- Splunk doesn't appear anywhere: not in the repo, the installed `@clevercloud/client`, or `docs/services-logs-drains.md`. You declined web access, so I couldn't check Clever Cloud's API docs, and `gh` isn't logged in, so I couldn't look for an issue.

If I guessed the API code and field names, the CLI would let users create drains the API rejects or sets up wrong. So I need these from you (or from the API spec or the API team):
1. The `recipient.type` value for Splunk (`SPLUNK`? `SPLUNK_HEC`?).
2. The name of the HEC token field (`token`? `hecToken`?), and whether it's required.
3. Any optional fields the API supports, such as `index`, `source`, `sourcetype` or TLS verification.
4. Whether the URL has to end with a particular path, like `/services/collector/event`, the way Elasticsearch drains have to end with `/_bulk`.
5. The issue number this work closes. `AGENTS.md` requires one for the PR.

**Plan once I have those**
- Add `SPLUNK: { apiCode, cliCode: 'splunk', label: 'Splunk' }` to `DRAIN_TYPES`.
- In `drain.create`, add a `--hec-token` option, or reuse an existing one if the API field matches. Check that it's set, along with any optional fields and URL rule, matching how the other drain types are handled.
- Show the Splunk-specific fields in `formatDrain`, but never the token.
- Add a "Splunk logs drains" section with an example to `docs/services-logs-drains.md`, add `splunk` to its list of drain types, and update `skills/clever-tools/SKILL.md` if it lists drain types.
- Run `npm run docs` and `npm run validate`, then check the result with `node bin/clever.js drain create --help`. I won't actually create a drain unless you confirm and the active profile is a test account.

If you'd rather I look it up myself, allow WebFetch for `clever-cloud.com` / `api.clever-cloud.com` and I'll get the API spec.
